column1: # The data surface, judged. One line per insert site in a migration that puts
# rows into a table holding the winery's records rather than the system's.
# The question for each: **would another winery installing this system have this
# row?** `universal` yes, and it ships. `local` no, it is this winery's own, and
# it belongs in a seed outside the repository. scripts/data-surface.py fails on
# anything unjudged, and on anything judged `local` that is still here.

IRS Schedule F, a public tax form, the same for every farm in the country, plus the money-in and transfer classes any set of books needs. What one winery adds to it is loaded from data/ by scripts/seed-terms.py.

One class meaning the transaction was looked at and deliberately not named. Universal because it is a fact about the state of the knowing rather than about how this farm is run: every set of books has money the bank line alone cannot explain. Without it such a row can never leave the unexplained pile and the count of that pile stops meaning anything.

One operation, prune. Every vineyard in the world prunes, so it ships. The seven neighbouring operations this vineyard also performs do not ship, because which distinctions a given operation draws between suckering, hedging, tying down and thinning is a fact about how that vineyard is run, and AR-E5 means each is later a row rather than a migration.

Three kinds of place: building, room, storage. Every operation has buildings, rooms, and somewhere inside a room where things sit. What this winery calls a particular one, Bay 3 or the woodshed or halfway down the sheds, is the location name and does not ship.

Three place tags: winery, tools, vineyard. Every installation of a winery management system has somewhere wine is made, somewhere tools live, and ground the fruit comes off. Which of this winery's rooms carries which does not ship: those are rows in location_tag written through the capability.

The gases a cellar puts over wine and the two ways wine moves between vessels. Air, argon, nitrogen and carbon dioxide are what any winery blankets with or fails to; gravity and pump are how wine moves anywhere. Which of them a given cellar keeps in a bottle is its own business and adding a fifth is a row.

One operation, dump. Every winery pours something away eventually, and until this there was no way to record it: rack refuses a transfer with no destination, correctly, so a dumped barrel had to be lied about or left full.

Why wine is dumped, loss or flaw, and the bulldog as a third way wine moves. Any winery loses wine by accident or pours it away because it went wrong, and a bulldog bung is standard cellar equipment. The words are categories rather than anything this cellar did.

Receipt, check, invoice, other, with how many days either side of its date a bank line can land. Every business that spends money has these four papers, and the windows are facts about how cards post and checks clear rather than about this winery.
How fruit was sorted: by hand, on a sorting table, by an optical sorter, or not at all. Any winery sorts one of these ways, and one more is a row added from the picker.

One operation, restate_shares: saying how a lot really divides between its sources when the pounds going in got it wrong. Any winery that co-presses fruit of different yields needs it, and the row records the kind of act, not any lot.
A third dump reason, over-counted, and the 2nd free run as a press cut. Any winery over-estimates a volume sometimes, and a 2nd free run is standard for reds pressed off skins.

Five settings, each off: whether cellar hands may register vessels and bins, add to the lists, arrange places, edit the vineyard, or edit the stores. Every winery with more than one login faces these questions, and the rows ship off, which decides nothing for anybody.

One operation, bins_moved: a bin recorded in the wrong part of a pick moved to the right one before weighing. Any winery picking two clones or two varieties at once puts a bin in the wrong part sometimes, and the row records the kind of act, not any pick.
One kind of reading, Brix, in degrees Brix: every winery measures sugar during a ferment and reads it the same way. Temperature is deliberately not added, because its unit is the winery's to say.
